title: Clean Fuel Protocol: How we designed for traceability of renewable fuels in the Dutch market with Digital Product Passports
subtitle: How a consortium designed a way to keep a renewable fuel's sustainability claim verifiable all the way to the buyer, instead of losing it the moment the fuel changes hands — now an annex to the Dutch government's RED-III completion letter to parliament.
featuredImageAlt: Renewable-fuel value chain from generation through production, storage and multimodal delivery, illustrating where a verifiable sustainability claim must survive downstream.
excerpt: Past the point where a renewable fuel is registered for national RED-III compliance, a company can barely claim more than a market-average reduction. This is the story of the Clean Fuel Protocol: a UNTP-based, voluntary Digital Product Passport for renewable fuels, set out by a consortium of the Centre of Excellence Digital Product Passports, TNO, Regen Studio and Fides for RVO, and now an annex to the government's RED-III completion letter to the Dutch House of Representatives (Tweede Kamer).
